jobs.excerpt: About WillowWillow is building the leading Operational AI platform for the built world.
jobs.description:
About Willow

Willow is building the leading Operational AI platform for the built world. We help owners and operators of large, complex environments better understand, manage, and optimize their buildings and infrastructure by connecting physical, operational, and human data into a unified digital foundation. Our platform enables customers to move from fragmented systems and reactive workflows to smarter operations, better decision-making, and meaningful financial and operational outcomes.

We are at an important stage of company growth: scaling commercial momentum, increasing operating rigor, and building the foundation for long-term category leadership.

About the Role

This role plays a critical part in delivering Willow's Digital Twin platform to customers.Working closely with project and team leads, you will help drive successful deployments, coordinate cross-functional activities, and ensure high-quality outcomes.This role offers the opportunity to grow and nurture strategic customer accounts and directly contributing to Willow's long-term growth and expansion.

Our ideal candidate is a self-starter with a demonstrated record of successfully coordinating complex, cross-functional projects to achieve desired outcomes. Previous experience working across subject matter areas where you may or may not be an expert will also be key to success.

Standout candidates will have a proven ability to understand and explain complex technical content to enable internal and external teams to arrive at appropriate decisions. This is an individual contributor role (not a people-management position) that sits within our Customer Engineering (CE) department, and it will require the ability to collaborate across cross-functional teams to support deployment efforts, build strong internal working relationships, and manage stakeholder expectations.

Responsibilities:

    • Help build and set up Digital Twins for our clients by working directly on live deployment projects
    • Use your knowledge of building systems (HVAC, BMS, electrical, and mechanical) to help process and validate data
    • Work with 3D building models (such as Revit or Navisworks) to understand building layouts and support accurate Digital Twin creation, while analysing large datasets using tools like Excel to identify issues and ensure data accuracy
    • Work closely with teammates across different departments to help set up and support system integrations.
    • Use AI tools to speed up data processing, documentation, and problem-solving, while staying open to learning and adopting new tools and technologies as they become available.
    • Ensure the Team Leader is informed on progress, issues, risks and blockers on a daily basis to enable accurate deliverable management
    • Engage with Willow’s Product and Engineering team to improve product capabilities and roadmap

What we are looking for:

    • 3+ years’ experience in MEP / building services engineering, Building Automation Services, or project/program coordination, ideally in a SaaS or technology-enabled services business
    • An MEP engineering background (mechanical, electrical and/or plumbing), specifically control and monitoring within the built environment, is highly valued
    • A solid understanding of typical building technology systems such as HVAC controls, Building Management Systems (BMS), lighting controls, energy metering networks, IT/OT/IoT devices and networks, and access control and security technologies
    • 3D modeling / BIM experience is highly regarded and a significant plus — exposure to authoring or review tools such as Revit, Navisworks or Archicad.
    • Comfortable using or learning AI tools like Claude to improve productivity
    • Strong communication skills — able to explain things clearly and simply to teammates
    • Strong data analysis skills, with the ability to interpret and work across large, disparate datasets (e.g. using Excel, SQL or similar tools) to draw out insights and inform decisions
    • A positive attitude, enthusiastic, flexible, energetic and highly motivated

Company Summary:

Slang.ai is redefining customer engagement through conversational AI, making every interaction seamless and efficient. Our mission is to transform the restaurant industry by providing the ultimate voice AI solution for consistently outstanding customer experiences. At Slang.ai, we foster a culture of innovation, inclusivity, and growth, ensuring that every "Slangsta" (employee) feels valued and connected to our broader AI driven impact.

What Your Experience Will Be:

As a Slang Ambassador in our referral program, you will have the unique opportunity to leverage your industry expertise and network to help restaurants discover the value of Slang.ai. Working directly with our Sales Director and Account Executives, you will play a vital role in our growth by introducing potential buyers to our team. Your role is flexible, impactful, and designed to reward you for successful outcomes.
You will begin with a personalized onboarding process, including training on Slang.ai’s value proposition, the tools we provide, and our ideal customer profile. Together, we’ll identify the best-fit restaurants for you to target, ensuring your efforts lead to mutual success.

Why You Belong Here & Why you will Grow:

At Slang.ai, trust forms the cornerstone of our relationships—both internally and externally. As a Slang Ambassador, you’ll embody this trust as the first point of contact for many potential customers. You’ll work closely with our team in a collaborative and supportive environment that prioritizes growth, inclusion, and learning.
This role is perfect for individuals who are well-connected in the restaurant industry and want a flexible, results-driven opportunity to contribute to an innovative company. You’ll gain firsthand experience in the world of AI-powered customer solutions and have the chance to deepen your industry expertise while being fairly compensated for your efforts.

What Success Looks Like:

  • Introductions Made: Actively identify and connect restaurants to Slang’s Account Executives via email introductions.
  • Demo Engagements: Help drive successful demos by making warm, trusted introductions.
  • Conversions: Facilitate successful deals by introducing restaurants with a high likelihood of adopting Slang.ai.
  • Compensation Earned: You will earn monetary rewards based on the number of successful deals closed from your referrals.

What You Will Bring:

  • Industry Expertise: A strong network in the restaurant industry, with proven connections to decision-makers.
  • Relationship Skills: Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to build trust quickly.
  • Entrepreneurship: A self-starter mindset with the ability to work independently and manage your time effectively.
  • Collaborative Spirit: A willingness to engage with Slang’s team and contribute to the program’s overall success.
  • Alignment with Our Mission: Passion for innovation and improving the customer experience in the restaurant industry.

How you will work

At Slang.ai, we understand the importance of flexibility and balance. As a Referral Partner, you will operate on your own schedule, with no strict time commitments. You will work remotely, using tools we provide for seamless collaboration and communication. Compensation is monetary and based on performance, offering a straightforward and rewarding engagement model.

Our Vision

Calling a business shouldn’t feel like a robot-hostage situation, where you’re forced to listen to horrible music and can't reach a human, while enduring a soulless voice uttering "I'm sorry I didn't quite get that" on repeat for eternity. (shudder) That’s why we started Slang.ai. We use the latest AI and audio wizardry to make transacting via voice so enjoyable it’s more human than human. By 2030, we will save businesses and consumers 1 billion minutes of precious time while transforming voice channels into the preferred mode of communication (it's faster and easier than text).
We have backgrounds building product at companies like Spotify, Buzzfeed, the New York Times, and OpenTable —shipping experiences that have reached hundreds of millions of users. Now, we’re using our backgrounds to start a new culture, one that puts product and human-centered design above all else while fostering constant learning and growth. jobs.description:
About Versapay

Versapay’s purpose is to remove financial friction so business ecosystems can transact smarter, faster, and with greater resiliency. We build cloud-based accounts receivable solutions that help finance teams accelerate cash flow, improve visibility, and operate with confidence. We are a remote-first organization across the U.S. and Canada. Our teams operate with a high degree of trust and autonomy, and we succeed because our people take ownership of their impact, communicate clearly, and follow through on commitments.

Our Values

  • Own Your Impact – Accountability is not negotiable. We take responsibility for outcomes, not just effort.
  • Show Grit – We persevere through ambiguity and challenge with resilience and determination.
  • Unite to Win – We create value with and for others, working respectfully toward shared goals.
  • Act with Courage and Candor – We give and receive feedback openly, knowing it makes us better.
  • Energize and Build Joy – We seek understanding, celebrate wins, and take care of ourselves and each other.

About Our Salesforce Platform

Salesforce is a mission-critical enterprise platform within our organization. We manage it with a strong emphasis on architectural discipline, governance, and long-term sustainability. We are hiring a Salesforce Developer who will work closely with our existing platform team and business stakeholders to ensure the platform remains scalable, secure, and reliable as we evolve. This is a high-ownership position within a mature, integration-aware environment.

The Role — Salesforce Developer (Integrations & Platform)

    This is an individual contributor role. You will lead your assigned integration design, build, and ongoing health work while sharing broader Salesforce platform delivery ownership with the team. You will work directly with vendor and partner technical teams, translate business needs into supportable designs, and build in the error handling, monitoring, and documentation that keep payment-adjacent workflows trustworthy. You will operate with a high degree of independence and partner closely with our team and business stakeholders.

    Key Focus Areas

    • Share ownership of Salesforce solution design, development, and support, including integrations between Salesforce, internal customer-facing applications, third-party vendors, and business partners supporting customer applications and ACH / credit card processing
    • Support the workflows behind merchant onboarding, transaction processing enablement, and customer billing
    • Build with Apex, Lightning Web Components, Flow, and platform APIs, choosing declarative or programmatic solutions deliberately
    • Design resilient error handling, retry, reconciliation, and monitoring patterns so integration failures are caught early and diagnosed quickly
    • Serve as the technical point of contact in vendor and partner conversations, from scoping through go-live and ongoing support
    • Reduce technical debt in legacy integration code and improve performance, testability, and supportability
    • Maintain clear technical documentation and support structured release, validation, and version-control practices

Who Thrives in This Role

    • You think ‘in’ systems, not just in Salesforce. You understand what happens on both sides of an integration, and you design with the downstream system, the data contract, and the failure mode in mind.
    • You own integration outcomes, not just your code. When something breaks between a partner and us, you help investigate, coordinate across teams and vendors, and drive your workstream toward resolution rather than routing a ticket onward.
    • You are credible in a room with a vendor. You can lead a technical conversation with an external partner, hold a design position, ask the questions that surface hidden assumptions, and keep the relationship productive.
    • You respect the weight of money movement. Payment and billing workflows leave no room for casual assumptions, and you bring the rigour, testing habits, and attention to data integrity that this work demands.
    • You communicate clearly across dev and business. You can talk design with engineers and outcomes with business stakeholders, tailoring the message to the audience. This is critical to the role.
    • You are a calm, trusted partner under pressure. You handle competing priorities, production issues, and candid feedback with composure, keeping stakeholders confident and focused on solutions.
    • This is your primary professional focus. A permanent, full-time, in-house role — not a contract or consulting engagement — for someone who wants to go deep on a single Salesforce org.
    • You build with AI. We actively encourage AI-assisted work. Wherever you are on that journey, we value curiosity, a willingness to fold AI into your workflow, and the judgment to validate its output.

Required Experience

    • 4+ years of hands-on Salesforce development experience in a professional environment
    • Demonstrated ownership of Salesforce integration work with both internal applications and external vendors or partners
    • Strong proficiency in Apex, Lightning Web Components, SOQL/SOSL, and Flow
    • Working command of integration patterns and APIs (REST, SOAP, Bulk, platform events), authentication models, and error-handling design
    • Experience with Salesforce DX, Salesforce CLI, Git-based source control, and CI/CD or structured deployment tooling
    • Comfort with admin-level configuration such as page layouts, validation rules, permission sets, and data model design
    • Strong systems thinking and independent, self-directed execution
    • Excellent, plain-language written and verbal communication with technical, business, and external partner audiences

Preferred

    • Fintech or payments background, including exposure to ACH, credit card processing, merchant onboarding, or billing — valued, but not required for the right candidate
    • Working knowledge of Salesforce CPQ / Revenue Cloud and Asset Lifecycle Management
    • Salesforce Platform Developer I, Administrator, or App Builder certification
    • Experience in a Scrum or Agile environment using Jira for sprint and support management
    • Experience working within structured governance and release models
    • Comfort using AI tools in day-to-day development work

To Apply

    Please begin your application by confirming that you are applying for the Salesforce Developer role, then complete the application and answer the short questionnaire.

jobs.description:
The Territory Sales Manager (TSM) is responsible for owning all sales activity within an assigned geographic footprint, including new business development, existing customer growth, and channel expansion. This role serves as the primary point of accountability for driving both run-rate business and larger project opportunities within the territory.

The TSM must balance aggressive hunting for new opportunities with disciplined coverage of existing customers, distributors, and integrators. While the TSM owns territorial execution, they work closely with Vertical Sales Managers to pursue prioritized vertical targets and ensure larger, strategic projects progress effectively.

This role requires strong end-user engagement skills, the ability to coordinate multiple stakeholders, and the discipline to pursue opportunities of all sizes—from smaller transactional wins to complex, multi-stakeholder system solutions.

  • Own all sales activity within assigned territory, including new business, existing customers, and channel partners.
  • Support representative firms through regular communication, business planning, sales coaching, and pipeline reviews.
  • Maintain active participation in organizations such as CANASA, ASIS, BOMA, IFMA, and other relevant industry groups.
  • Actively hunt for new opportunities while maintaining consistent focus on run-rate and small-to-mid-sized projects.
  • Develop and expand relationships with end users, systems integrators, distributors and architects, engineers & consultants (ACE) within the territory.
  • Identify, qualify, and drive complex video security opportunities involving multiple stakeholders.
  • Execute against vertical targets assigned by Vertical Sales Managers and provide regular updates on project progression.
  • Maintain disciplined opportunity management and provide timely status updates using approved sales tools (e.g., Blue Sheets).
  • Collaborate closely with Regional Directors and Vertical Sales Managers to align territory execution with vertical strategy.
  • Travel within the territory (50-70%) as needed to support customer meetings, partner engagement, and key opportunities.
  • High School diploma is required. A Bachelor’s degree in Business, Marketing or technical discipline is preferred.
  • 5 years of industry experience, preferably with a manufacturer, is required.
  • Proficiency with CRM platforms and Microsoft Office applications.
  • Industry affiliations and certification a plus.
  • Strong communication skills, solid industry and product specific knowledge, plus the ability to successfully generate and close business.
  • Industry certifications or involvement with organizations such as CANASA, ASIS, BOMA, IFMA, or equivalent associations preferrred.
  • French language proficiency is considered an asset but is not required for the position.
  • Requires 50-70% travel and requires that the individual reside within the district they represent.
  • Must reside in Canada and be legally eligible to work.

The Canada based salary range for this full-time role is $85,000-$90,000 CAD annually. This role is also eligible for commission. Within the range, individual pay is determined based on several factors, including, but not limited to, work experience and job knowledge, complexity of the role, job location, etc.

In addition to base salary, full-time employees are eligible to participate in Keenfinity Group's CAN Health and Welfare Benefit Plans—including medical, dental, vision, disability, and life insurance—as well as the company’s RRSP plan, subject to the terms and conditions of the respective plan documents. jobs.excerpt: About VersapayVersapay’s purpose is to remove financial friction so business ecosystems can transact smarter, faster, and with greater resiliency.
jobs.description:
About Versapay

Versapay’s purpose is to remove financial friction so business ecosystems can transact smarter, faster, and with greater resiliency. We build cloud-based accounts receivable solutions that help finance teams accelerate cash flow, improve visibility, and operate with confidence. We are a remote-first organization across the U.S. and Canada. Our teams operate with a high degree of trust and autonomy, and we succeed because our people take ownership of their impact, communicate clearly, and follow through on commitments.

Our Values

  • Own Your Impact – Accountability is not negotiable. We take responsibility for outcomes, not just effort.
  • Show Grit – We persevere through ambiguity and challenge with resilience and determination.
  • Unite to Win – We create value with and for others, working respectfully toward shared goals.
  • Act with Courage and Candor – We give and receive feedback openly, knowing it makes us better.
  • Energize and Build Joy – We seek understanding, celebrate wins, and take care of ourselves and each other.

About Our Salesforce Platform

Salesforce is a mission-critical enterprise platform within our organization. We manage it with a strong emphasis on architectural discipline, governance, and long-term sustainability. We are hiring a Salesforce Developer who will work closely with our existing platform team and business stakeholders to ensure the platform remains scalable, secure, and reliable as we evolve. This is a high-ownership position within a mature, integration-aware environment.

The Role — Salesforce Developer (Integrations & Platform)

    This is an individual contributor role. You will lead your assigned integration design, build, and ongoing health work while sharing broader Salesforce platform delivery ownership with the team. You will work directly with vendor and partner technical teams, translate business needs into supportable designs, and build in the error handling, monitoring, and documentation that keep payment-adjacent workflows trustworthy. You will operate with a high degree of independence and partner closely with our team and business stakeholders.

    Key Focus Areas

    • Share ownership of Salesforce solution design, development, and support, including integrations between Salesforce, internal customer-facing applications, third-party vendors, and business partners supporting customer applications and ACH / credit card processing
    • Support the workflows behind merchant onboarding, transaction processing enablement, and customer billing
    • Build with Apex, Lightning Web Components, Flow, and platform APIs, choosing declarative or programmatic solutions deliberately
    • Design resilient error handling, retry, reconciliation, and monitoring patterns so integration failures are caught early and diagnosed quickly
    • Serve as the technical point of contact in vendor and partner conversations, from scoping through go-live and ongoing support
    • Reduce technical debt in legacy integration code and improve performance, testability, and supportability
    • Maintain clear technical documentation and support structured release, validation, and version-control practices

Who Thrives in This Role

    • You think ‘in’ systems, not just in Salesforce. You understand what happens on both sides of an integration, and you design with the downstream system, the data contract, and the failure mode in mind.
    • You own integration outcomes, not just your code. When something breaks between a partner and us, you help investigate, coordinate across teams and vendors, and drive your workstream toward resolution rather than routing a ticket onward.
    • You are credible in a room with a vendor. You can lead a technical conversation with an external partner, hold a design position, ask the questions that surface hidden assumptions, and keep the relationship productive.
    • You respect the weight of money movement. Payment and billing workflows leave no room for casual assumptions, and you bring the rigour, testing habits, and attention to data integrity that this work demands.
    • You communicate clearly across dev and business. You can talk design with engineers and outcomes with business stakeholders, tailoring the message to the audience. This is critical to the role.
    • You are a calm, trusted partner under pressure. You handle competing priorities, production issues, and candid feedback with composure, keeping stakeholders confident and focused on solutions.
    • This is your primary professional focus. A permanent, full-time, in-house role — not a contract or consulting engagement — for someone who wants to go deep on a single Salesforce org.
    • You build with AI. We actively encourage AI-assisted work. Wherever you are on that journey, we value curiosity, a willingness to fold AI into your workflow, and the judgment to validate its output.

Required Experience

    • 4+ years of hands-on Salesforce development experience in a professional environment
    • Demonstrated ownership of Salesforce integration work with both internal applications and external vendors or partners
    • Strong proficiency in Apex, Lightning Web Components, SOQL/SOSL, and Flow
    • Working command of integration patterns and APIs (REST, SOAP, Bulk, platform events), authentication models, and error-handling design
    • Experience with Salesforce DX, Salesforce CLI, Git-based source control, and CI/CD or structured deployment tooling
    • Comfort with admin-level configuration such as page layouts, validation rules, permission sets, and data model design
    • Strong systems thinking and independent, self-directed execution
    • Excellent, plain-language written and verbal communication with technical, business, and external partner audiences

Preferred

    • Fintech or payments background, including exposure to ACH, credit card processing, merchant onboarding, or billing — valued, but not required for the right candidate
    • Working knowledge of Salesforce CPQ / Revenue Cloud and Asset Lifecycle Management
    • Salesforce Platform Developer I, Administrator, or App Builder certification
    • Experience in a Scrum or Agile environment using Jira for sprint and support management
    • Experience working within structured governance and release models
    • Comfort using AI tools in day-to-day development work

To Apply

    Please begin your application by confirming that you are applying for the Salesforce Developer role, then complete the application and answer the short questionnaire.

AHEAD builds platforms for digital business. By weaving together advances in cloud infrastructure, automation and analytics, and software delivery, we help enterprises deliver on the promise of digital transformation.
At AHEAD, we prioritize creating a culture of belonging, where all perspectives and voices are represented, valued, respected, and heard. We create spaces to empower everyone to speak up, make change, and drive the culture at AHEAD.
We are an equal opportunity employer, and do not discriminate based on an individual's race, national origin, color, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, religion, age, disability, marital status, or any other protected characteristic under applicable law, whether actual or perceived.
We embrace all candidates that will contribute to the diversification and enrichment of ideas and perspectives at AHEAD.

AHEAD is looking for an experienced, people-focused engineering leader to lead the team behind Hatch and Unity. We’re a leading IT services provider, trusted by some of the world’s largest companies to design, build, run, and modernize their most important technology across cloud, data, AI, and security.

Hatch is an advanced platform for IT lifecycle management, renewal, procurement, and logistics, giving enterprises real-time visibility and control over their IT assets, orders, contracts, and inventory across thousands of sites. Unity, its sibling platform, extends those capabilities to streamline our own operations and service delivery. You’ll lead a progressive engineering team that lives on the forefront of technology: one that builds real products, adopts new tools early, and never stops learning. Keeping that team curious, growing, and shipping is the heart of the job.

You’ll own the health, growth, and performance of the team while partnering with product and business stakeholders to deliver features that drive real value for our customers. This isn’t a purely administrative role. We’re looking for someone with strong technical instincts who can guide architectural decisions, remove blockers, and help the team do their best work. Your success will be measured by the success of your team and the impact of the products they deliver, built the way the best teams build software today.

Leading in the Age of AI

    AI has changed what great engineering looks like, and we’re building accordingly. We’re looking for a leader who sets the standard for using it well, encouraging the team to treat AI tools and coding agents as a force multiplier while holding a high bar on review, testing, and ownership. As AI takes on more of the routine, a team’s edge comes from judgment, product sense, and the discipline to verify what ships. You’ll cultivate exactly that.

    • Champion fluent, responsible use of AI tools and agents, so the team delivers faster while staying firmly accountable for quality and security.
    • Hire and develop for judgment, product sense, and verification skills, not raw output.
    • Shape the team’s AI workflows, tooling, and standards, and keep improving them as the landscape shifts.

What will you be doing?

    • Lead, mentor, and grow a team of software engineers building the Hatch and Unity platforms.
    • Partner with product management and business stakeholders to translate requirements into actionable development plans.
    • Own delivery timelines and ensure the team ships high-quality software on schedule.
    • Conduct regular 1:1s, provide feedback, and support career development for your team members.
    • Participate in hiring efforts: sourcing, interviewing, and onboarding new engineers.
    • Foster a healthy team culture built on collaboration, accountability, and continuous improvement.
    • Guide technical discussions and help the team make sound architectural decisions.
    • Remove obstacles and shield the team from distractions so they can focus on building.
    • Establish and refine development processes and AI-assisted workflows, balancing agility with predictability.
    • Collaborate cross-functionally with operations, customer success, and other engineering teams.
    • Stay close enough to the codebase, and to how the team works with AI, to give meaningful input during code reviews and technical planning.

What does the ideal Candidate look like?

    • 5+ years of software development experience, with at least 2 years in a management or team-lead role.
    • Experience managing teams building web applications, ideally in Elixir/Phoenix or similar modern stacks.
    • A strong understanding of software development practices: testing, CI/CD, code review, and Agile methodologies.
    • Fluency with modern AI development tools, and a clear point of view on how they change the way teams build, hire, and measure impact.
    • A proven ability to hire, develop, and retain strong engineering talent. Increasingly, that means hiring for judgment, product sense, and verification skills, not raw output.
    • Excellent communication skills, with the ability to translate between technical and non-technical audiences.
    • Experience managing delivery across multiple products or initiatives simultaneously.
    • Comfortable with ambiguity and able to make decisions with incomplete information.
    • A track record of building trust with both your team and cross-functional partners.
    • A genuine interest in the growth and well-being of the people you manage.
    • Familiarity with REST and GraphQL APIs, database design, and cloud infrastructure is a plus.
    • Experience in B2B SaaS, supply chain, or IT asset management is a plus, but not required.

Why You'll love it here

    • Lead a team building the platforms that enterprises rely on to manage their IT.
    • Real influence over how we build. Your technical instincts and process ideas will shape the team’s direction.
    • Significant, ongoing investment in modern tooling, including the best AI tools, and in the people who use it.
    • Competitive salary, comprehensive benefits, and genuine respect for work-life balance.

Make your voice heard

    AHEAD recognizes the value of diverse perspectives. The way you’ve built and led teams, including your wins and your hard-won lessons, will shape how ours grows. Tell us how you think about leadership, what a healthy engineering culture looks like to you, how you believe great teams should build with AI, and the work you’re proudest of helping your teams deliver.

Through our daily work and internal groups like Moving Women AHEAD and RISE AHEAD, we value and benefit from diversity of people, ideas, experience, and everything in between.

We are on a mission to eliminate bottlenecks and revolutionize the food and beverage CPG supply chain by developing innovative, all-in-one software that starts with the contract manufacturer.
Contract manufacturers and contract packagers (collectively, co-packers) are facilities that have extra production capacity and provide their services for a fee to customers (brands). Co-packers play a vital role in the trillion dollar U.S. Food and Beverage (F&B) Consumer Packaged Goods (CPG) industry, providing a range of services to convert raw materials into finished goods. These facilities are responsible for blending, drying, baking, frying, forming, and milling raw materials into bottles, pouches, cans, and other packages for our favorite foods and drinks. They are vital businesses for all food and beverage brands, including the thousands of emerging food and beverage brands that lack the resources to handle manufacturing on their own.
We’re building vertical B2B SaaS for F&B manufacturers to run all aspects of their daily operations from estimating costs and ordering raw materials to tracking inventory, managing communication with food and beverage brands, and automating production tasks. Chef Robotics is bringing AI into the physical world, starting with one of the world’s largest industries: food manufacturing.

Food production faces one of the most severe labor shortages in the US, with more than 1 million open jobs today and demand continuing to grow. Our robots help manufacturers automate repetitive food-preparation and assembly tasks so they can increase throughput, improve consistency, and keep production onshore.

Today, Chef robots operate in production facilities across North America and Europe, serving customers including Amy’s Kitchen, gategroup, and CookUnity. Our robots have made over 100 million servings in production, creating the world’s largest proprietary dataset for AI-powered manipulation of deformable food. Every meal our robots produce makes the system smarter.

Backed by leading investors including Avataar Ventures, Construct Capital, Bloomberg Beta, Promus Ventures, and Kleiner Perkins, we’re scaling rapidly with a robotics-as-a-service (RaaS) model and long-term customer partnerships. Our team includes engineers and leaders from Google, Cruise, Tesla, Amazon Robotics, Dexterity, Bear Robotics, Saildrone, and Zoox, united by a mission to build intelligent machines that solve meaningful problems in the real world.

If you’re excited about solving hard problems, creating real customer impact, and shipping systems that operate in production every day, not just in the lab, you’ll feel at home at Chef.

About The Role

As a Key Account Executive, you will own the full sales cycle, from outbound discovery and demos to complex negotiations and closing. You will be a foundational member of our enterprise team, shaping how enterprise sales are built at Chef Robotics.

What You’ll Do:

  • Manage multi-stakeholder buying processes within large-scale food manufacturing and contract manufacturing firms.
  • Drive enterprise-grade deals with an average contract value (ACV) ranging from $100K to $1M.

Who You Are:

  • You have a proven track record of navigating complex organizations and closing deals that move the needle for the business.
  • You thrive in high-stakes environments and are motivated by closing six-figure enterprise deals.
  • You are excited by the prospect of deploying AI and robotics to solve critical labor challenges in the food industry.
  • You enjoy the "inflection point" stage of a startup—where the product is proven, but there is still significant room to shape the direction of the company.

Why Join Us Now?

  • We are in a sector that has been slow to adopt automation but is now moving fast.
  • Join a team heading into a Series B with a pipeline that is already outgrowing our current capacity.

Our robots are already operating in production facilities every day, generating the real-world data that powers the next generation of embodied AI. If you want to build technology that leaves the lab, ships to customers, and transforms an industry, Chef is the place to do it.

About HexCoded

HexCoded is an AI video studio: you should be able to make anything you can imagine. We are a very small team in Gurgaon building the tools that are reshaping how video, image and audio get made.

What you'll actually work on

  • Growth and GTM. Run outbound and paid experiments end to end — build the list, write the copy, send it, read the numbers, kill what does not work. You will own campaigns, not assist on them.
  • The numbers. Own the funnel from signup to first paid render. Find where people fall out, tell us why, and be specific enough that we can go fix it.
  • Users. Talk to them — on calls, on chat, in their own words. Bring back what they actually said, not a summary of what we hoped they said.
  • Product. Break things before customers do. Test what is about to ship, write the bug that gets fixed, and argue for the change you think matters.
  • Market. Know every tool in our space better than its own marketing page does — what it costs, what it does better than us, and where we win.
  • Whatever is on fire. Some weeks that is a vendor, a spreadsheet, a hiring pipeline or a launch. This is the honest part of the job.

What you'll bring

  • You are already an AI generalist, whether or not you have called it that. You use these tools daily, you know which one to reach for and where each falls over, and you have built something with them that you were not qualified to build. Being able to write a little code with a model’s help goes a long way here — you do not need to be an engineer.

  • Comfort with numbers. Spreadsheets do not scare you, and neither does being wrong in public when the data says so.
  • Clear, short writing. Most of your output is words other people act on. Long and vague is worse than short and wrong.
  • Speed over polish. You would rather ship ten rough things this week than one perfect thing next month.
  • Final-year student or a 2026 graduate. Any degree.

    • How to apply

  • Apply through this posting — it takes two minutes, and we read every one.

HexCoded is an AI video studio: you should be able to make anything you can imagine. We are a very small team building the tools that are reshaping how video, image and audio get made. Check out hexcoded.ai

What you'll actually work on

  • Make the content. Reels, shorts, posts, hooks, thumbnails, captions. Most of it made in HexCoded itself, posted in public.
  • Run our editors. We work with a bench of freelance video editors. You write the brief, pick the reference, chase the deadline, and send it back when it isn't right. Content nobody chases doesn't get made.
  • Fill the Discord. We have one. It's nearly empty. Getting people in there and keeping it alive is yours — inviting them, welcoming them by name, starting the conversation on the quiet days, and telling the rest of us what those people actually want from us.
  • Write the emails. All of them. The hello when someone signs up. The nudge that gets them to make their first ad. The note to people who drifted away. The announcement when we launch something. You write it, you send it.
  • Write the ads. You'll sit with the ad account, see which ads are doing well, and write the next batch. You won't control the budget. You'll be the one who knows why the winner won.
  • Watch the numbers. Views, saves, Discord joins, replies, signups. Not for a report. Because you can't get better at this without knowing which of your posts worked and which died.

What you'll bring

  • An account you've actually run. Yours, a friend's, a college club's, a page about something you love. Send us links and real numbers, including the posts that flopped.
  • Taste you can explain. Show you two thumbnails and you can say which one wins and why, in a sentence. "It just feels better" is where you start, not where you stop.
  • You already build things with AI. Not a chat tab you ask questions in. Actual work. You've had a model rename two hundred clips at once, pull a week of numbers into one place, write thirty versions of a caption so you could pick the best one, or make some small thing that saves you an hour every day. You'll do a lot of that here, including in Claude Code, which is Claude running on your computer where it can work on your files directly. You don't need to know it already. You do need to have used AI to save yourself real time, and be able to show us what you made.
  • Short, clear writing. Most of what you make is a few words a stranger reads once and judges us on.
  • You're properly online. You knew what happened on Instagram this week before anyone told you. You can name a format that died and say what killed it.

jobs.title: Principal Backend Engineer
jobs.excerpt: Jeeves is a groundbreaking financial operating system built for global businesses that provides corporate cards, cross-border payments, and spend management software within one unified platform.
jobs.description:
Jeeves is a groundbreaking financial operating system built for global businesses that provides corporate cards, cross-border payments, and spend management software within one unified platform. The company operates across 20+ countries including Brazil, Canada, Colombia, Mexico, the United Kingdom, across Europe, and the United States, and serves over 5,000 clients ranging from venture-backed startups to SMBs around the world. With a mission to empower businesses with more efficient and cost-effective financial solutions worldwide, Jeeves combines cutting-edge financial technology with exceptional team expertise to transform the business financial landscape. Jeeves has been recognized as one of The Information's 50 Most Promising Startups in 2023, as well as a Y Combinator Top Company 2021-2023 and won “Fintech of the Year" at the European Fintech Awards.
Since graduating from Y Combinator in 2020, Jeeves has successfully raised over $380 million and is backed by top world-class investors including Andreessen Horowitz, Y Combinator, CRV, Tencent, Stanford University, Clocktower Ventures, and founders of more than 15 unicorns including David Velez (Nubank), Carlos Garcia (Kavak) and Sebastián Mejía (Rappi).
Jeeves is looking for a Senior Backend Engineer to join our LATAM engineering team. You will design and build the backend systems that power Jeeves's financial platform — working across payments, cards, spend management, and compliance infrastructure that serves businesses across the Americas and beyond.
This is a backend engineering role at its core, we're looking for a strong backend engineer who knows how to work effectively with AI tools, understands where AI can accelerate development and product capabilities, and is comfortable integrating AI-powered features into production backend systems.
Given the global nature of our business and the collaborative nature of our team, fluency in English is required for daily work with engineering, product, and business teams across multiple regions. Fluency in Spanish or Portuguese is equally required — our LATAM teams, customers, and operational partners work in both languages, and you will too.
Location: This is a full-time remote position.

What You'll Do:

    Backend Engineering

  • Design, build, and maintain scalable, reliable backend services that process financial transactions and serve Jeeves customers across 20+ countries.
  • Write clean, testable, production-quality code in Go, Python, or Node.js/TypeScript; participate actively in design and code reviews.
  • Build and consume RESTful and GraphQL APIs; design inter-service communication using gRPC, message queues, and event-driven architectures.
  • Design and optimize relational and non-relational database schemas (PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Redis) for correctness, performance, and scale.
  • Own backend features end-to-end — from scoping and technical design through deployment, monitoring, and iteration.
  • Implement security best practices: authentication, authorization, input validation, and data protection across distributed services.

    • AI-Assisted Feature Development

  • Integrate LLM API calls (e.g., OpenAI, Anthropic) into backend services as product features — such as spend categorization, document parsing, or natural language workflows — ensuring those integrations are reliable, observable, and cost-efficient.
  • Build backend pipelines that consume AI-generated outputs safely: validate structured outputs, handle fallback scenarios, and design graceful degradation when AI services are unavailable or return low-confidence results.
  • Collaborate with AI and data science teams to integrate model outputs into backend APIs — bridging experimental AI work and production systems.
  • Use AI coding tools (GitHub Copilot, Claude, Cursor, etc.) fluently as part of your everyday development workflow.

    • Reliability & Operations

  • Instrument services with structured logging, distributed tracing, and metrics for full operational visibility.
  • Participate in on-call rotation; respond to production incidents and contribute to post-incident reviews.
  • Contribute to CI/CD pipeline improvements, testing infrastructure, and deployment practices.

    • Cross-Regional Collaboration

  • Work closely with engineering, product, compliance, and data teams across multiple time zones and regions — communicating in both English and Spanish or Portuguese as the situation requires.
  • Contribute to a globally distributed engineering culture through thorough documentation, async design reviews, and thoughtful pull request feedback.
  • Bring your regional perspective to product and engineering conversations — our LATAM customers have specific needs, and engineers who understand those markets make our product better.

Requirements:

    Minimum Requirements

  • 5+ years of professional backend engineering experience building and operating production systems.

  • Fluent in English — professional fluency required for daily work with global teams in written and spoken contexts.

  • Fluent in Spanish or Portuguese — required for collaboration with LATAM teammates, customers, and operational partners.

  • Strong proficiency in at least one backend language: Go, Python, or Node.js/TypeScript.

  • Experience designing and building RESTful APIs, microservices, and event-driven backend systems.

  • Solid understanding of relational databases (PostgreSQL preferred): schema design, query optimization, and data modeling.

  • Experience with cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP, or Azure), containerization (Docker, Kubernetes), and CI/CD pipelines.

  • Demonstrated ability to integrate third-party APIs reliably in production — including error handling, retry logic, and observability.

  • Experience working on globally distributed teams across time zones and regions.

  • Comfortable using AI tools as part of everyday engineering work — integrating LLM API outputs into backend services and using AI coding assistants fluently.

    • Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in fintech, financial services, payments, or a regulated industry — familiarity with ledger systems, payment rails, or financial compliance (KYC/AML, PCI-DSS) is a strong plus.

  • Prior experience at a startup or high-growth scale-up, comfortable building in ambiguity without heavy process support.

  • Experience with multi-currency systems or cross-border payment processing.

  • Familiarity with message queue systems (Kafka, RabbitMQ) and event-driven architecture.

  • Global work experience — prior roles at companies operating across multiple countries and regulatory environments.

  • Fluency in both Spanish and Portuguese is a meaningful additional asset.

jobs.title: Staff AI Operations Lead
jobs.excerpt: What We’re BuildingHoneycomb is a service for the near and present future, defining observability and raising expectations of what developer tools can do!
jobs.description:
What We’re Building

Honeycomb is a service for the near and present future, defining observability and raising expectations of what developer tools can do! We’re working with well known companies like HelloFresh, Slack, LaunchDarkly, and Vanguard and more across a range of industries. This is an exciting time in our trajectory, we’ve closed Series D funding, scaled past the 200-person mark, and were named to Forbes’ America’s Best Startups of 2022 and 2023!
If you want to see what we’ve been up to, please check out these blog posts and Honeycomb.io press releases.

Who We Are

We come for the impact, and stay for the culture! We’re a talented, opinionated, passionate, fiercely inclusive, and responsible group of bees. We have conviction and we strive to live our values every day. We want our people to do what they truly love amongst a team of highly talented (but humble) peers.

How We Work

We are a fully distributed company, which means we believe it is not where you sit, but how you deliver that matters most. We invest in our people and care about how you orient to our culture and processes. At the same time we imbue a lot of trust, autonomy, and accountability from Day 1.

About the problem space

AI has changed what's possible in go-to-market, support, and business operations. The constraint is no longer "can we build it" — it's "can we deploy it into a real workflow, prove it made things better, and keep it working."

Most companies are stuck at the demo stage: a lot of clever prompting, very little that runs reliably on Tuesday morning without someone watching it. This role exists to get us past that, everywhere outside of engineering.

Little more about the team:

You'll sit on the Data team, which is where this work belongs. Our team already operates at the seam between the business and its systems — we partner daily with RevOps, Customer Success, Sales, and Product, and we own the data infrastructure these workflows depend on. AI-in-the-business is a data problem with a model attached, and you'll have the pipelines, the warehouse, and the domain relationships already in place.

What you'll do

You are a senior individual contributor. Your job is to take business workflows that are slow, manual, or inconsistent, and make them fast, automated, and measurably better — then do it again, and leave behind enough shared scaffolding that the third one is easier than the first.

Ship automated workflows end to end

  • Partner with department leaders to identify the highest-leverage workflows in their orgs, and go deep enough on how the work actually happens to know where a model helps and where it doesn't.
  • Define success before you build: cycle time, quality, cost, risk. Instrument it. Report on it honestly, including when the answer is "this didn't work."
  • Deliver working systems, not prototypes, with evaluation harnesses, human-in-the-loop review where the stakes call for it, and ongoing monitoring.
  • Iterate on adoption the way a product manager would: user research, documentation, and a real plan for getting people to use the thing.

Build the shared substrate as you go

  • Establish patterns for model access, orchestration and agents, prompt and tool management, evaluation, logging, and cost control — derived from what real workflows needed, not designed in advance.
  • Build on the Data team's existing infrastructure rather than standing up parallel systems.
  • Co-own shared components with your counterpart in Engineering; identify dependencies early and bring them into partner roadmaps collaboratively.

Make the company fluent

  • Create templates, playbooks, and golden paths: prompt patterns, agent patterns, safety checklists, evaluation patterns.
  • Run office hours, demos, and community-of-practice sessions that make adoption feel accessible rather than intimidating.
  • Develop enablement material for distinct audiences — GTM, operations, leadership — from fundamentals through advanced workflows.
  • Help people build judgment about AI: when to use it, when not to, and how to tell whether it worked.

Keep it safe and governable

  • Partner with Security, IT, and Legal on access control, data handling, vendor risk, and policy — so that employees have a clear, fast, safe path to experiment.
  • Work with the Data team to apply our data classification standards to AI use cases: what data can be used for retrieval and context, and what audit trails are required when sensitive data flows through LLM pipelines.

What you'll bring

  • Deep experience shipping systems into real business workflows — you've owned something end to end, in production, that non-technical people depended on daily.
  • Hands-on fluency with modern AI stacks: LLMs, retrieval, tool use and agents, evaluation, guardrails — plus the pragmatism to keep things shippable.
  • The ability to learn someone else's job well enough to improve it. This role lives or dies on understanding how support, sales, or finance actually work.
  • A track record of leading cross-functional initiatives without formal authority, bringing clarity, momentum, and crisp decision-making.
  • Comfort navigating security, privacy, and compliance tradeoffs in real organizations: data classification, retention, access controls, vendor risk.
  • Strong teaching instincts — you explain complex things simply, write clear docs, and meet people where they are.
  • Demonstrated ability to stay current as the landscape shifts, and to change your mind in public when the evidence does.

Nice to have

  • SQL fluency and comfort in a modern data stack (dbt, a cloud warehouse, BI tooling).
  • Experience with workflow automation or enterprise systems: case management, ticketing, CRM, knowledge bases.
  • Familiarity with observability practices for AI systems: monitoring, quality signals, evaluation pipelines, cost and latency analysis.
  • Change management experience across a distributed, multi-function company.
  • Interest in external evangelism — writing, speaking, podcasts, peer groups.
Base Salary based on level of experience
$225,000—$265,000 USD

What you'll get when you join the Hive:

  • A stake in our success - generous equity with employee-friendly stock program
  • It’s not about how strong of a negotiator you are - our pay is based on transparent levels relative to experience

The role

We're seeking Robot Software Systems Engineers who thrive at the intersection of robotics systems and software architecture. If you're at home in ROS, enjoy wrangling complex software stacks, and can bridge the gap between research-grade algorithms and production robotics—let's connect!

You should be comfortable with ROS ecosystems, familiar with classical robotics packages (planning, perception, control), and have solid backend development skills. The core of this role involves integrating new algorithms and capabilities into our robotics software stack, ensuring everything works reliably together, and building the systems that support our robot learning pipelines.

Your work will span building integration layers between learning algorithms and robot hardware, developing monitoring and control infrastructure, creating simulation and testing frameworks, designing backend services for our robotics workflows, and help shape our overall technical architecture.


About Imitation Machines

Imitation Machines has an ambitious goal of bringing the latest advances in Imitation and Reinforcement Learning, Robotics and AI into an integrated platform that enables anyone in the world to create robot new and custom behaviours.

Imagine the state of future technology where anyone can teach any robot, by demonstration, to solve any task they need, and create intelligent robotic workforce that meets unique needs across industries, robot forms, and environments. We want this future to happen. We see that all the necessary technological prerequisites are in place, and we're building that future. The readiness of reinforcement learning, imitation learning, and robot hardware has reached a tipping point, positioning Imitation Machines to transform how robot behaviours are created. Rather than relying on conventional programming, we can radically accelerate the process and start building systems where robots are taught by human teachers through demonstration.

We're taking a practice-first approach: real-world robot deployments with our industry partners guide our research and development. By working directly with industries, robot developers, and system integrators, we position ourselves at the frontier of practical imitation learning—tackling the challenges that emerge when these technologies meet real applications. This makes us early integrators of imitation learning in production environments, and it's how we're paving the way for broader adoption of robotic automation.

Imitation Machines is a pre-seed funded startup moving quickly toward our next milestone. We're laser-focused on proving our vision and building a team of machines learning and robotics engineers who want to push the boundaries of what's possible in robot learning.


What we’re looking for

  • Experience with ROS/ROS2

As a key member of our execution team, you will ensure that all compliance projects are structured, tracked, and reported in strict accordance with our corporate PMO Standards.

This role provides the critical project management, compliance oversight, governance, and auditability necessary to keep all teams aligned and audit-ready.

1. PMO Reporting & Project Standards

  • PMO Standards Alignment: Manage and structure all compliance, security, and certification project plans, trackers, and document repositories in accordance with established PMO methodologies and guidelines.

  • Platform Management: Maintain up-to-date program trackers, schedules, and resource planning artifacts within central PMO tools (such as Asana or Jira) to ensure a single source of truth.

2. Hybrid Project Management & Governance

  • Milestone & Critical Path Tracking: Establish clear, phase-gate project plans for upcoming audits, mapping out the critical path for audit readiness, dry-runs, evidence lock-down, and formal evaluation windows.

  • Requirements Translation: Translate complex, rigid compliance controls (e.g., security protocols, data-filtering standards) into clear, actionable technical specifications, user stories, and development tasks.

  • Engineering Alignment: Partner with Security, TechOps, Data, and Engineering teams to slot compliance-related tasks and vulnerability remediations into active development cycles (sprints or Kanban) without disrupting the core product roadmap.

jobs.excerpt: About Whistic Whistic is a risk operations platform that helps security and compliance teams assess, monitor, and manage third-party vendor risk.
jobs.description:
About Whistic

Whistic is a risk operations platform that helps security and compliance teams assess, monitor, and manage third-party vendor risk. We combine automated assessments, continuous monitoring, and compliance controls to replace slow, manual risk processes with intelligent workflows.

Our values are Extreme Ownership, Customer Focused, Driven by Results, and Do What's Right, Speak Up.

The Role

You will be Whistic's only dedicated BDR, with one primary objective: build qualified pipeline.

This is not an entry-level SDR role. We're looking for an experienced Senior BDR who has already proven they can create pipeline through outbound prospecting and is ready to own that motion with a high degree of independence.

You know how to prioritize accounts, break into buying committees, cold call effectively, multi-thread the right people, and develop an account over time. You understand that great outbound is not just activity. It takes judgment, persistence, creativity, and knowing when to change the approach.

We provide the ICP, target accounts, positioning, and resources. You bring the experience and hunger to turn them into pipeline.

You'll also work inbound leads and support field events, but your success will be driven primarily by your ability to proactively create opportunities.

This is a fully remote, U.S.-based role reporting to our Head of Product Marketing, with travel for events and team meetups.

What You'll Do

Build and Develop Pipeline

  • Own outbound pipeline generation across Whistic's target accounts.
  • Prioritize accounts, identify the right buyers, and determine the best path to engagement.
  • Cold call daily and prospect across phone, email, LinkedIn, video, and other channels.
  • Build and maintain prospect lists using Clay, market research, intent signals, firmographic data, and trigger events.
  • Identify net-new accounts that fit our ICP and develop them into qualified opportunities.
  • Multi-thread 5+ contacts across InfoSec, GRC, risk, procurement, and vendor management.
  • Build account strategies around likely champions, economic buyers, blockers, compelling events, and entry points.
  • Develop accounts over time rather than treating a lack of immediate response as a dead lead.
  • Test and improve outbound messaging, sequences, and plays based on what is actually creating pipeline.
  • Use Claude, ChatGPT, Gong, and other tools to improve research, personalization, and call preparation.

Operate Like a Senior BDR

  • Bring your own point of view on how to prospect, prioritize accounts, and develop pipeline rather than waiting for a daily playbook.
  • Know the third-party risk landscape and Whistic's competitive position well enough to hold credible business conversations.
  • Recognize buying signals, uncover pain, and know when an opportunity has enough substance to bring in an AE.
  • Partner with AEs on priority accounts and provide clean handoffs with pain, stakeholders, context, and next steps.
  • Know your funnel, identify where it is breaking, and make adjustments without waiting for someone else to diagnose it.
  • Bring buyer feedback, objections, competitive intelligence, and messaging insights back to Sales and Marketing.

Support Inbound and Events

  • Qualify inbound leads quickly and with good judgment.
  • Support pre-event outreach, onsite conversations, and post-event follow-up to turn events into pipeline.

What You'll Need

  • 4–5+ years of B2B SaaS pipeline generation experience, including at least 2 years in an outbound-first role.
  • A documented record of exceeding pipeline or meeting targets.
  • Proven experience personally breaking into target accounts and turning cold outreach into qualified pipeline.
  • Strong cold-calling experience and the willingness to pick up the phone every day.
  • Experience developing and multi-threading complex accounts over time, including conversations with senior buyers.
  • Strong judgment around account prioritization, messaging, and where to invest your time.
  • Ability to operate independently. You should already know the fundamentals of outbound prospecting and be ready to own and improve your approach.
  • Experience with modern GTM tools such as Clay, Salesloft or Outreach, Salesforce, LinkedIn Sales Navigator, Gong, and Zoom.
  • Active use of AI tools such as Claude or ChatGPT for research, personalization, messaging, and call preparation.
  • Strong written communication and disciplined CRM hygiene.
  • Experience working trade shows or field events.
  • Ability to travel as needed.

Nice to Have

  • Experience selling into InfoSec, GRC, compliance, risk, or vendor management teams.
  • Experience prospecting into enterprise buying committees.
  • Experience at a growth-stage SaaS company.
  • Experience improving outbound systems, plays, or prospecting processes.
  • Experience operating as the only BDR or SDR on a team.
  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience.

How Success Is Measured

  • Outbound pipeline created against monthly and quarterly targets.
  • Qualified opportunities that advance after AE handoff.
  • Net-new target accounts developed into pipeline.
  • Multi-threading and penetration across priority accounts.
  • Qualified meetings held, with an emphasis on quality and conversion.
  • Build and maintain your own prospect lists in Clay, layering firmographic, technographic, and trigger data behind every contact

Benefits

  • Stock options
  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance
  • Company paid life insurance
  • Internet and wellness stipend
  • Mental health benefit
  • Paid parental leave
  • 18 Paid Holidays
  • 15 Days PTO (All available your 1st day) + 2 additional days each year of employment!
  • 3 Whistic DNA Days - Company-paid "Family Day", "Self Day", & "Community Day"
  • Whistic Fridays- Work ends at 3:00 PM every Friday
  • A world-class culture and employee experience!

How Success Is Measured Whistic's DEIB Commitment

Whistic is a place where you can be you.

It’s impossible to separate what you do from who you are, and we don’t want you to. In fact, we want just the opposite. When Whisticians share the richness of their experiences, personal connections are deepened, new levels of collaboration are unleashed, and our product innovation accelerates. We become unstoppable.

Whistic is committed to growing diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging across three key dimensions:

  • Workforce Representation: Hiring and retaining a diverse team
  • Fairness: Equitable rewards, recognition, and opportunities based on merit
  • Inclusive Culture: Fostering an inclusive culture where differences are celebrated

jobs.description:
The salary range for this role is $5,000 - $9,500 per month (Gross in USD)

About Sezzle:

With a mission to financially empower the next generation, Sezzle is revolutionizing the shopping experience beyond payments, blending cutting-edge tech with seamless, interest-free installment plans that make shopping smarter and more accessible. We’re not just transforming payments; we’re redefining how people discover, interact with, and purchase the things they love while driving real impact on merchant sales through increased conversions and higher order values. As we continue to shape the future of fintech and retail, we’re building an innovative, dynamic team passionate about creating more than just a transaction but a truly unique shopping journey. If you’re excited about pushing boundaries in tech and delivering a game-changing experience for consumers and merchants alike, come join us at Sezzle and help create the future of shopping!

Compensation:

For this senior role, with 6+ years of experience, the compensation range is $5,000 - $9,500 USD based on experience level per month and in gross amount. This range acknowledges the strong expertise and significant contributions expected at this level. This is a fully remote role. We believe the best engineers can do world-class work from anywhere, and we hire accordingly. Work from where you do your best work.

About the Role:

We are seeking a hands-on Senior Software Engineer, Security Platform, to build and own the platform the security team runs on: the services that discover, scan, triage and route security findings, the event-driven bus that connects them, and the CI security gates every team's pipeline runs through.

This is a development role on the security team, not a security-analyst role. Most of your time goes into designing, building and operating services in Go and Python on Kubernetes: new services where the programme needs them, the existing fleet where it has grown faster than its upkeep, and the NATS-based event platform that moves findings, inventory changes and notifications between them. The security gates in our GitLab CI (SAST, SCA, secret detection, container and IaC scanning) and the agentic triage and review workflows are part of that platform, not the whole of it. Your job is to make these systems fast, low-noise, and reliable enough to be trusted by default without slowing delivery.

You will report to the Director of Information Security and work alongside the engineers who own detection and response and network and zero trust — your platform is what their work composes with.

At Sezzle, AI-assisted engineering is a standard part of how we build. In this role you will build reusable agentic workflows (Claude Code skills, CI review agents, automated triage and verification) that multiply what the team can cover, and hold that review discipline in the platform code you own.

What You’ll Do:

  • Design, build, and operate security engineering services primarily in Golang and Python, on AWS and Kubernetes: new services where the programme needs them, and the upkeep, hardening and retirement of the existing ones.
  • Own the event-driven platform between the security services: the NATS bus, its contracts and consumers, delivery guarantees and observability — so a finding, an inventory change or an alert reaches every service that acts on it.
  • Integrate the platform end-to-end: scanners → finding system-of-record → tickets → metrics, so remediation state is visible and exam evidence is a by-product of engineering.
  • Own delivery of the security gates — SAST, SCA, secret detection, container and IaC scanning: scanner selection and tuning, suppression workflow mechanics, false-positive burn-down, and the rollout tooling that takes a gate from advisory reporting to enforcing without blocking delivery.
  • Build agentic security workflows: CI review agents, automated finding triage and verification, remediation helpers — tooling other engineers actually adopt.
  • Build the triage-to-remediation automation: validate true positives by hand enough to prove the tooling right, then automate the loop — reproduction context, fix guidance, and routing to the owning teams and to vulnerability-management operations.
  • Participate in threat modeling and secure design reviews for the services you build and the pipelines you own.
  • Participate in the on-call rotation for the services you own.

What We Look For:

  • 6+ years of professional software engineering experience, including significant backend experience.
  • Deployed significant changes to a production application in the past 30 days.
  • Strong proficiency in Golang, plus working proficiency in Python.
  • Hands-on experience building and operating event-driven or message-based systems (NATS, Kafka, or similar): contracts, idempotent consumers, replay, back-pressure.
  • Hands-on experience building and operating CI/CD pipeline tooling — jobs, shared templates, runners — GitLab CI at fleet scale is a strong plus.
  • Hands-on web application security knowledge: the OWASP Top 10 in real code — able to find these issues, fix them yourself, and encode the detection so they stop recurring.
  • Hands-on experience with SAST, SCA, and secret-scanning tooling (e.g., Semgrep, CodeQL, Snyk, Trivy, Grype, gitleaks), including tuning them to a signal-to-noise ratio developers will tolerate.
  • Demonstrated AI-forward engineering: you actively use AI tooling (e.g., Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or custom LLM integrations) in your development work today, have opinions grounded in practice about where it helps and where it doesn't, and have built agentic workflows that other engineers adopted.
  • Working knowledge of AWS and Kubernetes as deployment targets for the services you build.

Preferred Knowledge and Skills:

  • Experience in fintech, payments, BNPL, or consumer lending, especially with systems in cardholder-data or regulated scope.
  • Working knowledge of PCI DSS and SOC 2 as they apply to software development and change management — the platform you build is what produces that evidence.
  • Software supply-chain integrity: SBOM pipelines, dependency governance, artifact signing and provenance (Sigstore, SLSA).
  • Familiarity with policy-as-code and admission control (OPA, Kyverno, conftest) — your gates compose with the cluster's runtime policy-enforcement layer.
  • Exposure to bug bounty or external vulnerability report triage — enough to know what the automation you build has to get right.
  • Experience with threat modeling at a system level.

About You:

  • You measure yourself by other teams' code - a fix you shipped is good; a vulnerability class that stopped appearing across the fleet is better.
  • You'd rather ship a gate than publish a policy - you know that enforcement changes behavior and documents do not, and you build the enforcement so well that engineers want to keep it.
  • You have relentlessly high standards - many people may think your standards are unreasonably high. You are continually raising the bar and driving those around you to deliver great results. You make sure that defects do not get sent down the line and that problems are fixed so they stay fixed.
  • You're not bound by convention - your success—and much of the fun—lies in developing new ways to do things.
  • You need action - speed matters in business. Many decisions and actions are reversible and do not need extensive study. We value calculated risk-taking.
  • You earn trust - you listen attentively, speak candidly, and treat others respectfully.
  • You have backbone; disagree, then commit - you can respectfully challenge decisions when you disagree, even when doing so is uncomfortable or exhausting.
    You do not compromise for the sake of social cohesion. Once a decision is determined, you commit wholly.
  • You deliver results - you focus on the key inputs and deliver them with the right quality and in a timely fashion. Despite setbacks, you rise to the occasion and never settle.

Sezzle’s Technology Stack:

  • Languages: Golang, Typescript, Python
  • Frontend: Typescript - React and React Native
  • Backend: Golang
  • Database: MySQL, Postgres, Elasticsearch
  • DevOps & Cloud: AWS, Kubernetes
  • Version Control: Git
  • CI/CD: Gitlab
  • Testing: Developer and AI-driven, focus on automated end-to-end, integration, and unit tests
  • Open Source: Sezzle is focused on using open source, and we build what we can before buying!

What Makes Working at Sezzle Awesome?

At Sezzle, we are more than just brilliant engineers, passionate data enthusiasts, out-of-the-box thinkers, and determined innovators; we are skilled musicians, yogis, cyclists, chefs, golfers, dog-lovers, and rock-climbers. We believe in surrounding ourselves with not only the best and the brightest individuals, but those that are unique and purpose-driven in all that they do. Our culture is not defined by a certain set of perks designed to give the illusion of the traditional startup culture, but rather, it is the visible example living in every employee that we hire.

Chainguard secures the software supply chain and Customer Platform is how every customer, partner, and internal product line actually connects to it. This team owns the APIs, entitlements, policies, and platform primitives that enable everything else. It's the first thing a customer touches and the integration layer every internal team depends on. We're looking for a Staff Software Engineer who owns hard problems end to end, moves without hand-holding, and can be the technical anchor for a team that touches every corner of the company.

  • Own features end-to-end: from design through implementation, rollout, and iteration, in close partnership with Product Management and the partner Chainguard teams.

  • Extend Chainguard's agentic AI foundation into customer-facing product experiences
  • Provide technical leadership and mentorship to senior and mid-level engineers; help the team break down ambiguity and build toward clear outcomes
